definition: Essentially different in kind or difficult to compare.
example: The festival brought together disparate musical traditions.
nuance: Disparate emphasizes difference in character, not merely distance or separation.
prompt: A study tries to compare groups with very different backgrounds.
options: The report combined data from disparate populations with markedly different circumstances.
The disparate populations were identical in every relevant respect.
The populations were disparate only because they were separated by a locked door.
The disparate families in the study pleaded for help after losing their jobs.
reasons: This sentence demonstrates the meaning: essentially different in kind or difficult to compare.
Identical groups are not essentially different.
Physical separation alone does not establish a difference in kind.
Pleading for help suggests the look-alike 'desperate'; this word means unlike, not hopeless.

practice.prompt: A school robotics team includes students with very different interests.
options: The club had disparate members, nearly forty of them crammed into the workshop.
The team blended disparate talents, from knitting to calculus, into one gripper arm.
Since all five members trained with one coach on the same drills, their skills were disparate.
The judges made disparate comments about the robot, mocking its wobbly wheels.
reasons: A large headcount says nothing about how different the members are from one another.
Knitting and calculus are skills of completely unlike kinds, which is exactly the right fit.
Identical training produces matching skills, the reverse of what the word describes.
Mocking remarks would be disparaging; this look-alike word describes unlike things, not insults.
